t.6.29.1: But Rāma, having set his mind on climbing Suvela and followed by Lakṣmaṇa, spoke these words to Sugrīva.
t.6.29.3: Let us all climb well this Suvela, this lord of mountains, adorned with hundreds of minerals; here we shall spend this night.
t.6.29.2: And Vibhīṣaṇa too, the devoted night-ranger who knew dharma and was versed in counsel and in proper procedure, he addressed with gentle and excellent words.
t.6.29.4: And we shall behold Laṅkā, the dwelling of that rākṣasa, the evil-souled one by whom my wife was carried off, a deed that will end in his death.
t.6.29.5: He by whom neither dharma nor proper conduct nor noble lineage was regarded, he by whom, with a base and demonic mind, that contemptible deed was done.
t.6.29.6: He is that vilest of rākṣasas at whose very mention my anger grows, the base one through whose offense I shall see the slaughter of the rākṣasas.
t.6.29.8: Thus taking counsel, and filled with anger toward Rāvaṇa, Rāma ascended Mount Suvela with its many-hued peaks to make his camp there.
t.6.29.7: Indeed, one man alone, having fallen into the grip of Time's noose, commits a sin, and yet through that man's base misconduct his whole family perishes.
t.6.29.9: And Lakṣmaṇa, attentive and intent on valor, followed him from behind, raising his very great bow together with its arrow.
t.6.29.10: After him climbed Sugrīva together with his ministers and with Vibhīṣaṇa, and Hanumān, Aṅgada, Nīla, Mainda and Dvivida as well.
t.6.29.12: These and many other swift-moving monkeys, mountain-dwellers inclined to the speed of the wind, climbed by hundreds that mountain Suvela where Rāghava was.
t.6.29.11: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Panasa, Kumuda, Hara, and Rambha, the leader of a troop,
t.6.29.13: But they, having climbed the mountain on every side in no long time, beheld upon its summit the city, as though suspended in the sky.
t.6.29.14: The leaders of the monkey troops beheld that beautiful Laṅkā, with its splendid gates, adorned with excellent ramparts and filled with rākṣasas.
t.6.29.16: Seeing the rākṣasas eager for battle, all those vānaras let out mighty roars there, while Rāma looked on.
t.6.29.15: And those foremost of the monkeys saw another rampart, formed by the dark night-rangers stationed along the heights of the ramparts.
t.6.29.17: Then the sun, reddened by the twilight, went down to its setting, and the night came on, with the full moon for its lamp.
t.6.29.18: Then Rāma, lord of the army of monkeys, honored by Vibhīṣaṇa, who greeted him with joy, dwelt at ease on the summit of Suvela together with Lakṣmaṇa, surrounded by the troops of the troop-leaders.
